description: New Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has previously been granted to introduce a new Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act, since the provisions in the Microfinance Act No, 6 of 2016 are inadequate to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for microfinance industry in Sri Lanka. Subsequent to the publication of the Bill prepared accordingly in the Government Gazette, 07 petitions had been filed in the Supreme Court by various parties against the said Bill. Taking into account the determination delivered by the Supreme Court on the said petitions and the guidance of the Parliamentary ‘Sectoral Oversight Committee on Mitigating the Impact of the Economic Crisis’, the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development and the Central Bank of Sri Lanka have paid their attention towards the formulation of a new Bill. Accordingly, the Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2025 08 11, granted approval to introduce a new Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Act. The clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Bill prepared by the Legal Draftsman. The Proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the said Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Bill in the Government Gazette and submit the same thereafter to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Programme for Granting a Cost of Living Allowance for children in institutional care or guardianship and street children
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025.06.16 for the implementation of a programme to pay a monthly cost of living allowance of Rs. 5,000/- for children in institutional care or guardianship and street children. Accordingly, provision of the benefits of the said programme, which has been named as 'Artha', has been commenced from July 2025. It appears that, the said benefit could be provided with effect from January 2025, so that Rs.1,000 million allocated for the 'Artha' programme for the year 2025 can be utilized for the maximum benefit of the children. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Women and Child Affairs to consider the date of commencement of the benefits of the 'Artha' programme as 2025 01 01 and to credit the outstanding benefits due from that date to the accounts of the children, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the supply of 2,200,000 vials of Biphasic Isophane Insulin Injection (Human) 30% Soluble 70% Isophane
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - International competitive bids have been invited for the procurement of 2,200,000 vials of Biphasic Isophane Insulin Injection (Human) 30% Soluble 70% Isophane Injection, a drug used in the treatment of diabetic patients. Two bids have been received for the same. Accordingly, based on the recommendation of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the contract for the supply of 2,200,000 vials of Biphasic Isophane Insulin Injection (Human) 30% Soluble 70% Isophane Injection, to the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, M/s M.J. Biopharm Pvt. Ltd., India, for a sum of US$3.98 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Phase I of the Eppawala, Giribawa, Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama Integrated Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been decided to initiate the Eppawala, Giribawa, Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama Integrated Water Supply Project as a solution to the spread of chronic kidney disease in the border areas of the Anuradhapura District and the Kurunegala District. Under the said project, it had been initially planned to cover 134 Grama Niladhari Divisions in 09 Divisional Secretariat Divisions, and considering the health risks and lack of safe drinking water in the affected areas, it has been restructured as the Eppawala, Giribawa, Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama Integrated Water Supply Project – Phase I. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Urban Development, Construction and Housing to implement the Eppawala, Giribawa, Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama Integrated Water Supply Project - Phase I, during the period of 2026-2029, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Calling for Expressions of Interest from interested investors for the Caustic Soda/Chlorine project in Paranthan
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Paranthan Chemicals Limited has already completed a feasibility study for the resumption of the Caustic Soda/Chlorine manufacturing plant at the premises where the Paranthan Chemical Factory was located and plans are being prepared to establish the factory at that location in the future. Paranthan Chemicals Limited currently imports chlorine and distributes throughout the country and since the total amount of chlorine required for the country's water treatment is imported, there is a risk of the entire water treatment system being disrupted in the event of disruptions to global supply chains. Also, the establishment of a chlorine production plant in the country has been identified as a nationally important task to ensure water security by minimizing the foreign exchange spent on chlorine import. It is also expected that the implementation of the proposed project will create about 95 direct employment opportunities and about 2,000 indirect employment opportunities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to call Expressions of Interest from local and foreign investors interested in implementing the proposed project as a Public Private Partnership project on the 30-acre land allocated to Paranthan Chemicals Limited from the land where the said company was located, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation of a section of the Southern Expressway from Kottawa to Dodangoda
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The section of the Southern Expressway from Kottawa to Dodangoda was opened for traffic in 2011 and no major repairs have been carried out so far. The expressway section from 0km to 19km and the expressway section from 19km to 34km have been identified as requiring urgent repairs under two (2) packages. Accordingly, the damaged expressway section from km 0km to 19km, covering a 19km stretch of 4-lane expressway, has been planned to be renovated under the Package 02. Bids have been invited from local contractors under the National Competitive Bidding Procedure and 05 bids have been received. The proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to award the relevant contract to        M/s Access-WKK Joint Venture, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for an amount of Rs.1,490.96 million, based on the recommendations of the Bid Evaluation Committee and the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Improvement of (B115) Embilipitiya-Panamure-Buluthota Road
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Sri Lanka has obtained a loan of US$ 40 million from the OPEC Fund for International Development to improve the Rakwana -Suriyakanda Road section of the Galle - Deniyaya - Madampe Road. There is a balance of about Rs. 1,000 million of that loan, and it has been planned to use that money and government funds to improve a currently dilapidated Road section of 9.62 km from Kolonna to Suriyakanda of the Embilipitiya -Panamura - Buluthota (B115) Road. The said road section provides access to several tourist attractions such as Sinharaja Forest, Maduwanwela Walawwa, Wavulpane, Gongala, Handapanagala, Buluthota Waterfalls and Morning Side, thereby boosting the tourism industry as well. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to utilize the balance provisions from the Rakwana - Suriyakanda Road Project to improve the Embilipitiya - Panamura - Buluthota Road section and to meet the remaining financial requirement through the funds of the Government of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of works of stalled sub-projects implemented through the “Nearest School is the Best School” Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A project to develop infrastructure facilities in schools called 'The Nearest School is the Best School' has been implemented during the period 2016-2020. At the beginning of the year 2025, out of the sub-projects initiated under the said project, 29 projects under the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education and 03 projects under the Provincial Education Departments remained to be completed. Due to these stalled projects, the school community is facing many problems, and the money spent on those works has also become a waste of money. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to resume the remaining construction works of the remaining construction projects initiated under the 'Nearest School is the Best School' project and complete them on a priority basis in the years 2025, 2026 and 2027, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of all works of the unfinished construction projects of the universities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Several projects implemented in the universities of Ruhuna, Rajarata, Sabaragamuwa, Wayamba, Sri Jayewardenepura and the Trincomalee campus of the Eastern University of Sri Lanka for construction of buildings and development of other infrastructure facilities required by the universities, have not been fully completed due to various obstacles encountered during the approved timelines of those projects. The remaining works of the projects where more than 75% has been completed need to be fully completed, in order to enroll more new students and improve academic facilities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to fully complete the said construction works on priority basis, by managing the budgetary provisions to be allocated in the years 2026, 2027 and 2028, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Creating a 'Government Super App' to enable the public to obtain the Public services through a single web application
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been observed that the current fragmented approach to Public Service delivery which requires disparate systems, multiple authentication processes and repeated data entry across various Government departments cause significant inconvenience to citizens. It has also been estimated that this causes an economic loss of over Rs.500 million annually. Therefore, it has been identified that the development of the 'Government SuperApp' covering a wide range of Public Services to citizens through a single application, in line with the Sri Lanka's Digital Economy Blueprint, as a strategic priority. This Project will develop a digital platform that will enable 14 million citizens of Sri Lanka of the age of 18 years and 2 million annual visitors to access Public Services seamlessly through a single interface, consolidating all Public Services into a single, user-friendly mobile and web application. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as Minister of Digital Economy to implement the 'Government SuperApp' Project in 02 phases at a total cost of Rs. 500 million during the period 2025-2026, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Policy for Older Persons in Sri Lanka
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted for the ‘National Charter and National Policy for Senior Citizens in Sri Lanka” in the year 2006. It has been recognized that the National Policy for Senior Citizens in Sri Lanka needs to be updated in line with the evolving global trends. Also, since the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs has predicted that the population aged 60 years or above will increase to 24.8% by the year 2052, it has been recognized that it is essential to promote and protect the welfare and rights of the elderly population. Accordingly, the ‘National Policy for Older Persons in Sri Lanka’ has been formulated enabling to facilitate the elders to live a socially, economically, physically and spiritually fulfilling life in line with the theme of ‘A Respectable Senior Citizen – A Meaningful Retirement’ under the National Policy Framework of the Government. Approval of the Cabinet was granted to the said National Policy presented by the Minister of Rural Development, Social Security and Community Empowerment.

description: Treaty on Transfer of Sentenced Persons between Sri Lanka and the Republic of the Philippines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Transfer of Offenders Act, No.5 of 1995 contains provisions to enable a citizen of another country convicted and sentenced to imprisonment by a court in Sri Lanka to serve his sentence in the country of which he claims to be a citizen. Similarly, the Act also provides for a Sri Lankan citizen who has been sentenced to imprisonment in a particular country, to be transferred back to Sri Lanka to serve his balance period of the imprisonment. Accordingly, it has been proposed to sign a Treaty between Sri Lanka and the Republic of the Philippines on the transfer of sentenced persons. The proposed treaty will pave the way for the prisoners to return to their home countries for social rehabilitation and reintegration into their societies. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to sign the proposed Treaty and thereafter ratify the same, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Signing a Treaty on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters between Sri Lanka and the Republic of Philippines
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The process of providing or seeking assistance by one State to another State in serving of judicial documents and gathering evidence for use in criminal cases is known as Mutual Legal Assistance. It is anticipated that entering into a formal Agreement on mutual legal assistance, will lead to a solid corporation and enables effective crime prevention, investigation, prosecution and suppression of crimes. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to sign an Agreement on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters between Sri Lanka and Philippine, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memoranda of Understanding between Sri Lanka and the Republic of Turkey on Agricultural Cooperation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Cabinet, at its meeting held on 2021.02.15, has granted approval to sign a Memorandum of Understanding on Agricultural Cooperation between Sri Lanka and the Republic of Turkey, taking into consideration the benefits for the development of Sri Lanka's agriculture through the establishment of mutual cooperation with the Republic of Turkey, which uses advanced technologies in the agricultural sector. Nevertheless, the relevant Memorandum of Understanding has not been signed yet. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to obtain the approval of the present Cabinet to sign the said Memorandum of Understanding, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Entering into Memoranda of Understanding on Educational Collaboration between Sri Lankan Universities and Foreign Universities
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
The proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to sign the following Memoranda of Understanding between the Sri Lankan Universities and Foreign Universities with a view to establishing higher education collaborations with Foreign Universities to elevate Sri Lankan Universities to higher positions in world ranking indices and to promote internationalization, was approved by the Cabinet. 

•	Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Kelaniya and the Polessky State University of the Republic of Belarus, valid for a period of 05 years.

•	Memorandum of Understanding between the University of Kelaniya and the Vladimir State University of the Russian Federation, valid for a period of 03 years.

•	Memorandum of Understanding between the Department of Polymer Science, Faculty of Applied Sciences of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and the Petroleum and Petrochemical College, Chulalongkorn University of the Kingdom of Thailand.

description: Social Security Contribution Levy (Amendment) Bill
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A Bill containing the amendments for the Social Security Contribution Levy Act, No.25 of 2022 has been prepared by the Legal Draftsman for the tax policy amendments proposed in the Budget 2025. The said Amending Bill has received the clearance of the Attorney General. Accordingly, the proposal made the President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the Social Security Contribution Levy (Amendment) Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter to submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Declaration of "a National Children's Day Week"
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Many countries, including Sri Lanka, celebrate 1st October as the "World Children's Day". This year, under the theme "Protect with Love - To Conquer the World", all institutions dealing with children have jointly planned to implement a series of national programmes for World Children's Day under the guidance of the Ministry of Women and Child Affairs and organization of the Department of Probation and Child Protection Services. The proposal made by the Minister of Women and Child Affairs to declare a "National Children's Day Week" starting from 2025-09-25 ending as at 2025-10-01, including the main national celebration and to implement the following programmes under the same, in parallel to national programmes for World Children's Day, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Providing compensation to the sugarcane farmers whose crops were damaged due to burning of sugarcane plantations at the Sevanagala Sugar Factory
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been reported that a group of people had set fire to the sugarcane plantations of the Sevanagala Sugar Factory owned by Lanka Sugar Company (Pvt) Ltd. on 16th, 20th, 21st, 22nd, 24th August and 04th and 05th September 2025. It has been estimated that, as a result of this, approximately 19,000 metric tons of sugarcane belonging to about 235 farmers have been damaged. Since the sugarcane destroyed by the fire should be grinded only within the first 24 hours, purchasing and grinding of the sugarcane destroyed by the fire has been completed by 2025-08-30. As a result, the farmers whose sugarcane plantations were damaged are in a great difficulty and the attention of the Government has been focused on providing them with compensation for the damaged plantations. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development; and the Minister of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development to appoint a committee comprising of officers of the Sugarcane Research Institute and Lanka Sugar Company (Pvt) Ltd. to obtain information on the specific quantities of sugarcane destroyed by fire and the sugarcane farmers whose crops have been damaged, and to provide a compensation of Rs.7,000/- per metric ton of sugarcane destroyed by fire to those farmers, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No.40 of 1988
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The following proposals were made in the Budget Proposals - 2025 to increase the Government revenue.  *	Increasing the Gross Collection Levy from 15% to 18%.  *	Increasing the Casino Entrance Levy imposed on Sri Lankan citizens from USD 50 to USD100. 

	Accordingly, a Bill has been prepared by the Legal Draftsman to amend the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No.40 of 1988, enabling to implement the said proposals. The clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the said Bill. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter to present the same in Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Appropriation Bill to Parliament - 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-09-08 to publish the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026 in the Government Gazette and present the same in Parliament. Accordingly, the following Programme of Parliamentary Sittings for the Appropriation Bill for the year 2026, prepared by the Office of the Leader of the House of Parliament was presented to the Cabinet by the Hon. Prime Minister and the concurrence of the Cabinet was granted for the same.  *	First Reading of the Appropriation Bill - 2025-09-26  *	Second Reading of the Appropriation Bill (Budget Speech) - 2025-11-07  *	Debate on the Second Reading - 2025-11-08 to 2025-11-14  *	Debate on the Third Reading (Committee Stage of the Budget) - 2025-11-15 to 2025-12-05  *	Division on the Third Reading - 2025-12-05

description: Appointment to the Post of District Secretary/Government Agent in the Administrative District of Batticaloa
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Mrs. J.J. Muralitharan, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, serving as the District Secretary/Government Agent in the Administrative District of Batticaloa, is scheduled to retire from the Public Service with effect from 2025-09-26. The proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to appoint Mr. J.S. Arulraj, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as the Secretary to the Governor of the Eastern Province, to the Post of District Secretary/Government Agent in the Administrative District of Batticaloa falling vacant accordingly, with effect from the said date, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulation of Laws to enable Sri Lankans living abroad for casting vote
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The sovereignty vested in the people as per Article 3 of the Constitution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka shall be exercised by the people as per the provisions of Article 4 at the election. The franchise has been limited to citizens residing in Sri Lanka and whose names are registered in the register of electors as per the election law. Under the current Acts on election, neither systems for voting nor laws have been formulated thereunder to cast votes by the citizens living abroad. However, many Asian countries such as India, Bangladesh, and the Philippines have formulated legal strategies to enable their citizens abroad to vote, and it has been recognized as a timely requirement for Sri Lanka to make such legal amendments. Accordingly, the concurrence of the Cabinet was granted for the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to take measures to appoint a Committee comprising of the Officials from the Election Commission, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism, the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government and other relevant Ministries and Institutions to examine the matters related to amending the existing laws or formulating new laws to protect the right to vote of citizens living abroad.

description: Procurement for essential medical supplies from the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation and Local Manufacturers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-12-02 to directly purchase 291 medicines and other medical supplies required for the year 2025 to the Medical Supplies Division from the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation, local manufacturers who have joint venture agreements with the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation, and local manufacturers who have entered into buy back agreements with the Ministry of Health and Mass Media. However, due to some medicine stocks being either unfit for use or had expired, the need to maintain buffer stocks, and the increase in the consumption of certain medicines, some of the orders placed on the basis of forecasts have not been sufficient, and it is necessary to obtain additional stocks of 123 items from among those medicines and other medical supplies. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award procurements for the purchase of locally manufactured medicines as follows, was approved by the Cabinet:

•	To award the procurement for the supply of 24 types of medicines to the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation, for a sum of Rs.1.148 billion.

•	To award the procurement for the supply of 68 types of medicines to the local manufacturers who have signed joint venture agreements with the State Pharmaceuticals Manufacturing Corporation, for a sum of Rs.4.159 billion.

•	To award the procurement for the supply of 62 types of medicines to the local manufacturers who have signed buy back agreements with the Ministry of Health and Mass Media, for a sum of Rs.5.116 billion.

description: Implementation of the Sustainable Tourism Sector Development Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Asian Development Bank has agreed to provide a loan of US$ 100 million to implement a Sector Development Programme in the tourism sector. The said loan consists of two (02) components, a policy component of US$ 70 million and an investment component. Under the investment component, it is expected to carry out development activities to enhance the tourism potential and carring capacity of the tourist destinations of Trincomalee and Dambulla (including the Sigiriya area), control tourist congestion, extend the length of stay and increase contribution to the regional economy through the tourism industry. The Ministry of Urban Development, Construction and Housing will function as the executing agency and the implementing agency for the projects falling under the said investment component. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism and the Minister of Urban Development, Construction and Housing to sign the relevant Loan Agreements to obtain the proposed loan, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Phase II of the Ruwanwella Water Supply Project
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The contract for the Ruwanwella Water Supply Project, funded by the Economic Development Cooperation Fund of the Korea Exim Bank and the Government of Sri Lanka, has been awarded to M/s Kolon Global Corporation, a Korean company. Although the project was scheduled to be completed in 2022, it could not be completed as scheduled due to the Covid pandemic, revisions to plans, adverse weather conditions and the economic crisis. The then Committee on Re-structuring and Accelerating Mega Projects has taken steps to phase this project into Phase I and II. Accordingly, the construction under Phase I of the Ruwanwella Water Supply Project has been completed using funds from the Korea Exim Bank and the Government of Sri Lanka and has now been handed over to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board by the contractor. The proposal made by the Minister of Urban Development, Construction and Housing to revise the total estimated cost for the Phase II of the said project as Rs. 2,147 million and to implement that phase using funds from the Government of Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting a feasibility study on minimizing the traffic congestion at the Lotus Intersection and Surrounding Areas
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Lotus Roundabout in Colombo has become a critical traffic bottleneck, especially during peak hours, and it has been observed that this is causing a traffic congestion in the urban transport network. With the full operationalization of the Colombo Port City and the Port Access Elevated Highway and completion of the major ongoing developments in the Colombo metropolitan area, this problem is likely to exacerbate. Taking those factors into consideration, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to select a consultancy firm following the approved procurement process, to conduct a comprehensive feasibility study to develop sustainable solutions to mitigate traffic congestion around the Lotus Roundabout area and improve connectivity with key adjoining corridors, including the ramps of the Port Access Elevated Highway and the Marine Drive Extension, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Completion of the balance work of the Kohuwala Flyover and recommencement of the construction work of the Gatambe Flyover
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The project for the construction of Kohuwala and Gatambe flyovers have been implemented with funds received under the Framework Agreement for Financial Cooperation signed by Sri Lanka with the Government of Hungary. Following the suspension of funding by the Exim Bank of Hungary, due to the economic crisis which prevailed in the country at that time, the construction of the Kohuwala flyover has now been completed under the contractor's funds and opened for traffic. However, pedestrians have to face difficulties as the at-grade roads have not been completed. Similarly, the construction work of the Gatambe flyover also remains suspended. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to complete the unfinished at-grade roads of the Kohuwala flyover and to resume the construction of the Gatambe flyover using local funds through the current contractor, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Paddy Purchasing Programme of the Government for the Yala Season 2025
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government has allocated Rs.6,000 million for the paddy purchasing programme of the year 2025, and the Paddy Marketing Board has purchased 43,891 metric tons of paddy from 16 districts, spending Rs.5,288 million out of which, as of now. The Paddy Marketing Board has made plans to purchase the paddy harvest from the Polonnaruwa, Anuradhapura and Trincomalee zones, which are currently being harvested, during the upcoming Yala season. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to obtain additional provisions to further implement the Programme of Paddy Purchasing from farmers during the Yala Season 2025 under the government's guaranteed prices, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Obtaining Grant Assistance of the Government of Japan for the Project for the Enhancement of Productivity in the Dairy Sector and for the Official Security Assistance to the Sri Lanka Navy
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Government of Japan has agreed to provide a Grant of Japanese Yen 963 million (approximately Rs. 1.94 billion), as Japanese Yen 463 million for the Project for the Enhancement of Productivity in the Dairy Sector and as Japanese Yen 500 million for the Project for Official Security Assistance to the Sri Lanka Navy, in the backdrop of long-standing cooperation between the two countries. Necessary equipment and technical assistance are due to be provided to improve the capacity of the Department of Animal Production and Health under the Project for the Enhancement of Productivity in the Dairy Sector, while donations are to be provided for the supply of drones for reconnaissance, surveillance and monitoring activities of the Sri Lanka Navy under the Project for Official Security Assistance to the Sri Lanka Navy. The President is scheduled to sign the Exchange of Notes and other documents related to these projects during his forthcoming state visit to Japan, and the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to pursue action accordingly, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a state-of-the-art building for the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences of the University of Jaffna
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In 2006, degree programmes in Allied Health Sciences were introduced in State Universities, and three BSc (Hons) programmes have been started in the fields of Medical Laboratory Science, Pharmacology and Nursing at the University of Jaffna. Currently, 952 students representing all ethnic groups are studying in the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences of the University of Jaffna in four subject areas (Medical Laboratory Science, Pharmacy, Nursing and Physical Education). Although Cabinet approval has been granted for the construction of a building for the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences in 2017, funds have not been received for it due to the financial crisis which prevailed at that time. In this backdrop, the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences in Jaffna is currently facing an acute shortage of infrastructure facilities. As such, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to construct a new five-storey building comprising of lecture halls, laboratories, tutorial rooms, a dedicated examination hall and an auditorium for the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences of the University of Jaffna, at an estimated cost of Rs.2,234 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a new Three Storied Building for the Primary Section of the Maliyadwa College, Kurunegala
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - At present, 4,617 students are studying in Maliyadeva College, Kurunegala, which was established in 1888. The primary section of the College is housed in three old single-storey buildings with tiled roofs, and the facilities available in the said buildings are inadequate for the students. Therefore, the need for a child-friendly building with modern facilities for the Primary Section has been identified. Accordingly, a new three-storey building with 24 classrooms, an activity room, three teachers' rest rooms and sanitary facilities on each floor has been planned for the said College. It is a construction project included in the approved National Investment Programme for 2026-2030. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, to implement the project of the construction of the said building during the period 2026-2028, under an estimated cost of Rs. 392 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of a Value-Addition Project under the Public Private Partnership for Graphite in Kahatagaha Mine
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Kahatagaha mine, which is spread over an area of about 102 acres, is the deepest graphite mine in Sri Lanka. The Kahatagaha mine is currently operated under Kahatagaha Graphite Lanka Limited, a fully state-owned company, which produces and exports the high quality graphite. It had been decided under the previous Government to restructure Kahatagaha Graphite Lanka Limited, and it was decided at the Cabinet meeting held on 2023 12 11 that action should be taken to implement a Value Addition Project for graphite in the Kahatagaha mine by an investor to be identified. However, no further steps have been taken accordingly. It has been found that the locally available technology is insufficient to determine the graphite reserves in the mine. Taking into account the above facts, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to revoke the Cabinet decision dated 2023 12 11 pertaining to restructuring of Kahatagaha Graphite Lanka Limited and call for Expressions of Interest by following the approved procurement procedure to implement the entire project of exploring the graphite reserves of the Kahatagaha mine, mining the graphite in the said mine, processing the graphite and adding value to the graphite, under the Public Private Partnership method, while retaining the ownership of the graphite in the Kahatagaha mine with the said Company and safeguarding the jobs of the employees currently working in the said mine, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the “Sathkaraye Shrama Sena” Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-15 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It is predicted that over 800,000 skilled personnel in various categories in the tourism and hospitality sector will be required to achieve the Government's strategic objective of attracting 05 million tourists annually to Sri Lanka by 2030. Nevertheless, due to the limited resources currently available in the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management, it is not possible to train such a number. Therefore, the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management has planned to conduct a 06-month vocational training programme at National Vocational Qualification (NVQ) Level 3, called ''Sathkaraye Shrama Sena'', utilizing the infrastructure and trainers of the Tertiary and Vocational Education Commission (TVEC) accredited public and private sector training institutions located island-wide. This training programme is to be implemented for interested youth to suit with micro, small and medium scale as well as large scale hospitality industry, by providing both theoretical knowledge and practical training. The proposed programme will be held in batches consisting of 30 students, covering 360 hours in 60 days, while maintaining the academic control and quality assurance by the Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management and it is estimated that the cost per head will be Rs.55,832.50. The proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism to commence the training for 20,000 youth from Samurdhi beneficiary families in the first phase of this programme using the funds allocated for the empowerment of Samurdhi beneficiaries under the Department of Samurdhi Development in the year 2025 and complete it in the year 2026, and thereafter to train the remaining 80,000 through public-private partnerships, inter-agency collaborations and co-funding models, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Submission of the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026 to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval had been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-07-01 to prepare the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026 prepared by the Legal Draftsman. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter to submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Commissioner General of Agrarian Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The term of office of Mr. U.B. Rohana Rajapaksha, who is serving as the Commissioner General of Agrarian Development, is scheduled to end on 2025-10-08. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to appoint Mr. R.A.D.S. Ranatunga, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as an Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources, to the post of Commissioner General of Agrarian Development with effect from 2025-10-09, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Ceylon Arts Council Act, No.18 of 1952 (Chapter 278)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Ceylon Arts Council has been established through the Ceylon Arts Council Act, No.18 of 1952 (Chapter 278) with the aim of promoting the fine arts, developing and encouraging indigenous arts and crafts, and providing advise to Government Departments, Regional Authorities and Institutions on any relevant matter. It has been identified that it is essential to introduce amendments to the current Arts Council Act in a manner that will enable it to maintain financial stability, including maintaining a sponsor fund for quality art research and production projects, based on the needs and expansions that have already arisen and are arising in the fields of art. It is also expected that the amendment of this Act will provide scope for intervention to ensure the professional security, dignity and well-being of artists. The Ceylon Arts Council has recommended several amendments in this regard. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the Ceylon Arts Council Act, No.18 of 1952 (Chapter 278) in order to achieve broader objectives and goals than those set at the time of establishment of Ceylon Arts Council, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulating a new law for foster care
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that there is currently no formal legal provision on foster care that covers all children in need of alternative care in Sri Lanka. Therefore, with the aim of implementing the concept of foster care (foster parenting), which is a family-based alternative care system that has become a timely need, the National Child Protection Authority has submitted a Concept Paper to establish a foster care mechanism. Through the said proposed mechanism, it is expected to implement the care programme under two main methods, namely the establishment of foster care and distance foster support. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Acting Minister of Women and Child Affairs to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to introduce a new law for foster care, based on the said Concept Paper, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No.5 of 1973
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No. 5 of 1973 has not been updated to reflect the current social and cultural trends. Today, with the advancement of communication technology, television, Internet and social media networks have spread rapidly among the people, in addition to newspapers and radio, which has had a strong impact on public life. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to amend the Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No.5 of 1973, by including provisions on the main issues of the requirement that the correction/agreement/order decided as a result of the examination conducted by the Press Council after a newspaper report was broadcast and disseminated through an electronic media should also be broadcast and disseminated by the electronic media in which the original report was broadcast and disseminated and the registration of electronic publications of printed newspapers/magazines or electronic newspapers or magazines published in the form of printed newspapers and the examination of complaints in respect thereof, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introducing a new National Statistics Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The main legal framework for conducting census in Sri Lanka is the Census Ordinance No.9 of 1900. The Statistics Ordinance No.44 of 1935 has established a comprehensive statutory framework for the collection, compilation, analysis and dissemination of official statistics in Sri Lanka. However, it has been identified that the current legal framework does not provide an adequate platform for the coordination of all producers of official statistics, the integration of administrative and alternative data sources or the adoption of governance arrangements that ensure independence, impartiality and quality assurance. Therefore, a committee comprising of officers of the Department of Census and Statistics, under the technical guidance of an expert from the United Nations Statistics Division, has prepared an initial draft of the National Statistical Framework that is globally consistent and nationally compliant, combining international expertized knowledge with local institutional knowledge. The proposed initial draft seeks to modernize and unify the legal framework for the production, coordination and control of official statistics in Sri Lanka and to establish a national statistical system comprising all the producers of official statistics. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a new Bill based on the relevant initial draft, repealing the Census Ordinance No.9 of 1900 and the Statistics Ordinance No.44 of 1935, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the 'Mission Olympics' programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has planned to implement the 'Mission Olympics 2028 - Journey to the Rings' programme to identify sportspersons who have demonstrated outstanding performance and those who may have Olympic aspirations in the future and provide them with the necessary financial and other facilities. Through this programme, sportspersons with the potential and talent to achieve international achievements in sports and win medals at the Olympic Games are to be identified and directed to long-term formal local and foreign specialized training. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports to implement the 'Mission Olympic' programme, enabling to sign contracts with such sportspersons up to the upcoming Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and to provide financial and other support for training, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-commencement of the currently suspended Health Care Infrastructure Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Due to the Covid-19 pandemic and the subsequent economic crisis, 33 ongoing development projects in healthcare institutions have been suspended. Considering the current state of healthcare infrastructure and the increasing demand for services, it is essential to complete those projects duly. It has been identified that the total cost estimates and project timelines of the relevant projects need to be revised, due to the suspension of the projects and the increase in the cost of construction materials and labor due to inflation, prior to the re commencement of 17 projects out of them.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to revise the total cost estimates of the said projects and extend the project timelines, based on the recommendations given by the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting the Presidential Media Awards Ceremony
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although a Presidential Media Awards ceremony has been held annually to encourage journalists aiming to maintain the contents and programmes in the electronic, print and web media in Sri Lanka in a responsible, independent manner and aligned to the expectations of the audience, the said award ceremony has not been held since 2019. The said awards ceremony has been planned to resume from this year, and applications have been invited for the same, with respect to the creations of the year 2023. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to hold the Presidential Media Awards ceremony on 2025-11-11 and to increase the cash prize awarded to a winner up to Rs.100,000 and the cash prize awarded for the lifetime achievement award, which is given only once in a lifetime, up to Rs.400,000, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a Water Treatment Plant with a capacity of 5000 cubic meters per day for the Avissawella Water Supply Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited following the National Competitive Bidding procedure for the construction of a Water Treatment Plant with a capacity of 5,000 cubic meters per day for the Avissawella water supply scheme. Ten bidders have submitted bids for the said procurement. Based on the recommendations of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee and the Procurement Appeal Board, the proposal made by the Minister of Urban Development, Construction and Housing to award the contract for the construction of a Water Treatment Plant with a capacity 5,000 cubic meters per day for the Avissawella water supply system, to M/s Sierra Construction Limited, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, was approved by the cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Dambulla Industrial Estate
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Under the "Regional Industrial Estate Development Programme" implemented by the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, 33 Industrial Estates have been constructed across the island as of now. Similarly, development work is currently underway in 07 new Industrial Estates. The Dambulla Industrial Estate has been identified as a dedicated Industrial Estate for food manufacturing and food packaging industries. For this purpose, a land in extent of 64 acres 02 roods 10.2 perches has been identified in the village of Elen Egodayaya, in the Dambulla Divisional Secretary's Division. It has been planned to develop 24 acres of land as the first phase for the proposed Industrial Estate and the remaining land in the second phase. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to allocate Rs.750 million from the provisions of the year 2025, for the development of the infrastructure facilities of the Dambulla Industrial Park and proceed with its future activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of additional provisions for Road Development Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Out of the provisions of Rs.14,000 million allocated for the improvements of rural roads through the budget estimates for the year 2025 and rural bridges,  Rs.11,500 million has been allocated for rural road development, and subsequently, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-08-11 to provide another Rs.5,000 million for the said program. The total value of projects identified for the implementation under the Rural Road Development Programme in each District by all the District Coordination Committees of the country is approximately Rs.26 billion. Taking these factors into consideration, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to allocate an additional provision of Rs.6,000 million for the Rural Road Rehabilitation and Improvement Programme by managing the local financing provisions allocated to the Ministry of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation for the year 2025.

description: Allocation of land plots from Regional Industrial Estates to set up new Industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The selection of investors for investment in Industrial Estates is carried out by the "Regional Industrial Service Committee" established in accordance with the provisions of the Industrial Promotion Act, No.46 of 1990 and the "Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry" appointed by the Secretary to the Ministry. Accordingly, the Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry has recommended the allocation of land plots as well, for 38 investment projects from among the 42 project proposals recommended by the Regional Industrial Service Committees. The total value of investments to be made by the said 38 investors is Rs.2,548.22 million, and it is also expected to generate about 1,559 direct employment opportunities through those industrial projects. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to provide land plots from the relevant industrial estates on lease basis for a maximum period of 35 years to the said investors, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ensuring the Sustainable Operation of Cascade System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A group of interconnected tanks that exist within small and medium catchment areas in the dry zone of Sri Lanka is known as a Cascade System. The Cascade System, a masterpiece of Sri Lanka's irrigation civilization, has been designated a World Heritage by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Protecting the Cascade Systems, developing them with a sustainable plan, and working to bring its benefits to society have been identified as a task that must be carried out at present. The Department of Agrarian Development has issued Circular No.06/2023 regarding the establishment of "Cascade System Management Committees" to facilitate the active participation of farmers and other stakeholders involved in economic activities related to these Cascade Systems, which protect social, economic and environmental balance, and to manage those systems while preserving them. The proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to issue a new Circular jointly by the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation and the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government, enabling to establish Cascade System Management Committees, to implement the Cascade System Management Plan and to further regularize  the implementation of the relevant Committee process at district and divisional level, by amending the aforesaid Circular instructions as appropriate, and to take action to introduce amendments to the Agrarian Development Act No. 46 of 2000 to legalize the provisions of the said Circular, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ratification of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-12-23 to sign the Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction and establish an Inter Ministerial Committee in that regard. Accordingly, Sri Lanka has signed the said Agreement on 2025-02-20 and if Sri Lanka becomes one of the first 60 States to ratify and bring the Agreement into force and a founding member State thereof, Sri Lanka would be able to accrue numerous benefits including conservation and sustainable use of ocean’s resources and the equitable sharing of benefits derived from them. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism for Ratification of the Agreement on Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Climate Finance Strategy of Sri Lanka (2025-2030)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka has been identified by the Global Climate Risk Index as a country highly vulnerable to climate-related extreme weather events. It is predicted that Sri Lanka will lose more than 2% of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) annually, due to the adverse effects of climate change. Therefore, it is estimated that the Government will need to invest approximately US$500 million annually to build climate-resilient infrastructure. The National Budget cannot afford that cost, which is about 0.5% of GDP. Therefore, a significant investment need to be made across various sectors of the economy particular in, renewable energy, agriculture, fishery industry and climate-resilient infrastructure, to mitigate and adapt to climate change. For this purpose, there is a need to create an environment that can attract green investments and mobilize private capital for climate-resilient and low-carbon sectors by introducing a more structured and formal approach to raising funds beyond traditional budgetary financing. Such an approach supports national climate priorities while also reaffirming Sri Lanka’s commitment to its international climate obligations. Focusing on these issues, the Department of External Resources and the Department of National Planning, with the participation of 35 Government institutions including the Ministry of Environment, the Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Department of Forest and in collaboration with the United Nations Development Programme, have prepared the “National Climate Finance Strategy of Sri Lanka (2025-2030)”. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the National Climate Finance Strategy of Sri Lanka (2025-2030) and thereafter to promote and implement the said Finance Strategy, was approved by the Cabinet.
